frequency_question: How often does a recipient state successfully establish domestic manufacturing of foreign complex guided weapons despite severe structural friction within the target timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes major complex missile technology transfers to allied states during active high-intensity conflicts since 1950. Excludes simple small arms or non-guided munitions.

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile series (US technology assistance)
India BrahMos joint venture (Russian technology transfer and domestic production)
Pakistan Al-Khalid tank / domestic guided weapons initiatives
South Africa Project Cheetah / armaments domestic adaptation under embargo
Iran domestic cruise missile production from reverse-engineered Kh-55

coverage_note: 5 major documented historical analogues; universe of wartime advanced missile localization is small.
known_gaps: Few exact analogues exist for Western cruise missiles being localized inside a European theater during an active invasion.
skeleton: 5 documented major complex weapons technology localization programs under severe geopolitical friction or wartime conditions.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 cases based on historical adaptation urgency.
validity_reason: Industrial and technological transfer friction dynamics change slowly over decades barring total collapse of international defense industrial bases.
